subject: Taxes
title: The First Tax Collectors
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The First Tax Collectors.

hook.text: Around 3000 BCE, Sumerian scribes pressed clay tablets recording grain taxes. Government began the moment taxes did.

buildup.text: Early taxes weren't money—they were labor and crops. Farmers gave a portion of their harvest to the temple.

discovery.text: Taxes funded irrigation, armies, and temples. Without them, Mesopotamian civilization couldn't have existed.

twist.text: Tax collectors were among the most hated people in every ancient society. Some things never change.

climax.text: Civilization and taxation were born together. You cannot have one without the other.

punchline.text: No taxes, no civilization. They were born together in Sumer.

quiz.question: What form did the earliest taxes take?
